title: Argument and Commentary
tagline: What an argument is, the claim, evidence, methods of reasoning, structure, refutation, the language of argument, commentary and editorials, reviews, and the examination essay
summary: An argumentative essay persuades by reasons, not by slogans, quotations or ornament. This course teaches how to form a clear claim, choose and use evidence, reason soundly by example, analogy, cause and comparison, organise an argument and answer the other side, and write in the forms readers meet every day — commentary, editorials and reviews — and looks critically at the formulas of the examination essay.
overview: The writing course the logic course was built to serve: turning premise–conclusion skeletons into finished prose that a sceptical reader will follow, test, and (ideally) revise.

It covers the whole production line: staking a claim, choosing and weighing evidence, reasoning methods, structure, refutation, style, and then three working genres—commentary, review, and the examination essay.

The Chinese argumentative tradition runs through every chapter: the Han policy essay, the Tang single-thesis 论, Liang Qichao's new prose, and today's exam room—Western argumentation theory is the skeleton key, not the landlord.
outcomes: Distinguish thesis, claim, topic, and slogan, and state a debatable claim in one sentence
Grade evidence by kind and strength, and cite it without cheating the reader
Choose reasoning methods (deduction, induction, analogy, example, cause) to fit the claim
Plan essays with proven structures (classical five-part, Toulmin, Rogerian) and know their failure modes
Refute responsibly: steelman, locate the load-bearing premise, concede what must be conceded
Write argumentative prose with disciplined connectives, concession, and emphasis
Draft commentary and reviews that carry an argument, not just a mood
Read the examination prompt as a contract and deliver against it under time pressure

chapters.summary: Finding a claim worth arguing, making it precise, and limiting its scope.

chapters.title: Evidence
chapters.summary: Facts, data, examples and authorities, how to check them, and how to quote honestly.

chapters.title: Methods of reasoning
chapters.summary: Argument by example, analogy, cause, comparison and reduction to absurdity, and their limits.

chapters.title: Structure
chapters.summary: Raising, analysing and resolving a question, and parallel, progressive and contrastive structures.

chapters.title: Refutation
chapters.summary: Stating the other side fairly, refuting its claim, evidence or reasoning, and conceding.

chapters.title: The language of argument
chapters.summary: Precision, qualification, tone and rhetoric in argument, and avoiding empty grandeur.

chapters.title: Commentary and editorials
chapters.summary: Short commentary on current events: the news peg, the angle, evidence and balance.

chapters.title: Reviews
chapters.summary: Reviewing books, films and exhibitions: description, analysis and judgement.

chapters.title: The examination essay
chapters.summary: The gaokao essay and the civil-service *shenlun*, their formulas, and how to write well within limits of time and format without empty formulas.

history.title: The furore of the policy essays
history.detail: Jia Yi's Guo Qin Lun diagnoses Qin's fall in rhetorical overdrive: the Han-led policy essay as argument by momentum.

history.title: Memoirs that argue
history.detail: Chao Cuo's essay on grain: a technical argument (incentives, prices) embedded in courtly cadence.

history.title: The single-thesis essay
history.detail: Han Yu's Shishuo plants one thesis and circles it with definitions, examples and objections.

history.title: The strategist's essays
history.detail: Su Xun and Su Shi: pick one angle, press it to the wall—angle is argument.

history.title: New prose, new audience
history.detail: Liang Qichao's Xinmin Shuo serialised: the periodical essay as mass persuasion machinery.

history.title: A manifesto that practises itself
history.detail: Hu Shi's essay on literary reform argues for plain argument in the plain style.

history.title: The layout of reasoning
history.detail: Toulmin's claim–ground–warrant–qualifier arrives from law; composition studies adopt it decades later.

history.title: The essay returns to the exam
history.detail: The gaokao resumes with argument prompts: a generation relearns written argument in ninety minutes.
